newsitem.title: USA: Farmstead sees return to profit by year end.
newsitem.headline: Farmstead sees return to profit by year end.

text.p: Farmstead Telephone Group Inc said Thursday that it expects its losses to shrink in the third quarter and that it anticipates returning to profitability by the end of the year.

The company attributed its second quarter loss primarily to the unprofitable performances of its wholly-owned subsidiary, Farmstead Asset Management Services, and the Cobotyx voice processing division.

In addition, it posted a one-time non-cash charge to operations of $362,000 in connection with the full write down of its investments and receivables in its international subsidiaries, Beijing Antai Communication Equipment Co Ltd and Telesolutions Inc.

Farmstead said its core business, the sale of Lucent Technologies products, remained strong with revenues for the three and six months ended June 30 up 33 percent and 31 percent respectively, over the comparable prior-year periods.

For the quarter, the company reported a net loss of $835,000, or $0.26 per share, on revenues of $6.06 million. In the same period in the prior year, the company reported net income of $202,000, or $0.09 per share, on revenues of $4.65 million.

"There's no question that results for the second quarter were below our expectations," Chairman and Chief Executive George Taylor said in a statement. "To counter this performance, we are aggressively repositioning our organization to focus on domestic Lucent Technologies opportunities, expanding our business possibilities by concentrating on our strengths, and minimizing the negative impact on operations from our unprofitable units."
